# Tryll Engine (https://tryllengine.com)

> Tryll is on-device AI middleware for game engines (Unity, Unreal Engine 5 and proprietary engines). It gives in-game characters a realistic mind: they understand natural language, remember what the player did and act accordingly, running on the player's GPU with no servers, no per-token fees, and no user data leaving the device. Built by game developers; Epic MegaGrants recipient, funded by Early Game Ventures. Tryll Engine is in open beta.

## What Tryll does

- **Smart NPCs**: characters that understand natural language, remember what the player did, and act accordingly
- **Real Talk**: speech-to-text and text-to-speech on the player's device, with voiced NPCs in many languages (including Korean and Japanese) without recording every line
- **Dynamic worlds**: you set the world and its rules; Tryll creates agents and keeps them within those rules
- **New genres**: game mechanics that weren't possible before

## Features

- **Basic NPC**: natural dialogue with no dialogue trees to script; voice in and out on the player's device, in many languages; roleplay guardrails that catch jailbreaks and out-of-world questions and answer them in character
- **Advanced NPC**: answers from your world's lore and quest data (and says so when it doesn't know); each player line scored for what your mechanic needs, such as charm, pressure or an offer, while your game decides what happens; moods the character carries into what they say and how they sound; actions and tools that your game checks before they happen; memory and conversation summaries that save with the game
- **Developer tools** in the Unity and Unreal editors: chat with a character by text or voice without building the game or entering Play mode; visual workflow graphs; Dialog Lab (one scripted conversation across prompts, models and seeds side by side, with checks on every reply); Agent Log (what every agent heard, which path it took and what it said while the game runs)
- **Performance and memory**: a talking agent fits in 1.6 GB of graphics memory, with speech on the CPU; small models write 100–250 tokens a second on a gaming GPU, many times faster than a character speaks; the Memory window shows how much RAM and graphics memory models and agents take

## How to get started

1. Install the plugin; a Tryll tab appears in the editor
2. Download an open model into the project; Tryll runs it on the player's GPU
3. Build an agent: connect lore, define its role and allowed actions, test it in the Dialog Tester

## Pricing

- **Free** until a shipped game passes $200k USD in gross revenue; then a 1% royalty. No seats, no per-token fees.
- Free for game developers, individuals and small businesses under $200k, and for educators and schools with no revenue limit
- **Extra services** (custom pricing): forward-deployed engineering, QA and evals, security guardrails, custom AI components

## System requirements

- **Developers**: Windows 10/11 64-bit; Unity 6+ or Unreal Engine 5.7+; NVIDIA, AMD or Intel GPU (8 GB VRAM recommended for local testing); 16 GB RAM; 10–20 GB disk for models
- **Players**: any GPU with 8 GB VRAM or more, which covers about 3 in 4 Steam PCs (Steam Hardware Survey, 07/2026). One build serves a richer or leaner model per machine.
- **Platforms**: Windows PC today; console and mobile runtimes on the roadmap
